svg.title: Consistent Hashing Ring: Architecture, Virtual Nodes, and Resharding Dynamics
svg.desc: Detailed architectural diagram of a consistent hashing ring showing 0 to 2^160-1 or 2^32-1 token space, clockwise key lookup, virtual nodes variance reduction from 100-200 vnodes down to 5-10% standard deviation, and anticlockwise affected key range during node addition and removal.
svg.text: Consistent Hashing Ring: Ring Math, Routing Dynamics, and Virtual Nodes
Clockwise Key Routing, Anticlockwise Resharding Invariants, and Variance Reduction via Virtual Nodes
In-memory tokens stored in sorted array / red-black tree (e.g. Java TreeMap).
Binary search ceilingEntry(hash(k)) takes O(log(N·V)) time; wraps to first token at ring tail.
Redistributes only range (S3, S4] from successor S0
• Keys in arc (S3, S4] previously routed to S0; now reclaimed by new node S4.
• All other nodes (S1, S2, S3) keep 100% of their existing keys without disruption.
• Theoretical moved keys: exactly 1/(N+1) = 1/5 = 20% vs. 80% under naive modulo!
Reallocates range (S0, S1] to successor S2
• Keys in arc (S0, S1] must be reassigned clockwise to immediate successor S2.
• Danger: Without virtual nodes, S2 absorbs 100% of S1's load, risking a cascading crash.
• Moved keys: 1/N = 1/4 = 25% of keyspace; other nodes (S0, S3) take 0% extra load.
3. Virtual Nodes (Vnodes): Skew Elimination & Variance Reduction Mechanics
Empirical Law: Relative Standard Deviation σ / μ ≈ 1 / sqrt(V)
Each server has exactly 1 position on the ring
• Severe partition imbalance; random token spacing
• Failure cascades: single successor absorbs all keys
Servers assigned multiple tokens: hash(S0_0), hash(S0_1)...
• Interleaved tokens balance key distribution evenly
• Node crash disperses keys across ALL surviving nodes
Assign 2x vnodes to 64-core vs 32-core hosts for a 2:1 traffic split.
1,000 nodes × 256 vnodes = 256k entries (~10 MB RAM, high gossip CPU).
Modern engines replace static vnodes with 1–10 GB dynamic tablets.
